models_evaluated: 8 blinded LLMs (not named in the abstract)

links.outcome: Demographic bias in LLM conversations on clinical vignettes, as rated by clinicians
links.effect: Demographic bias was present in 82 conversations (9.8%) of 835 reviewed.
links.quote: Demographic bias was present in 82 conversations (9.8%), hallucinations in 85 (10.2%), classification errors in 19 (2.3%), and safety risks in 78 (9.3%).

links.outcome: Hallucination rate in LLM responses to clinical vignettes
links.quote: Demographic bias was present in 82 conversations (9.8%), hallucinations in 85 (10.2%), classification errors in 19 (2.3%), and safety risks in 78 (9.3%).

links.outcome: Safety risks in LLM responses to critical care, overdose, and psychiatric vignettes
links.effect: Safety risks in 78 conversations (9.3%), most prominent in overdose, critical care, and psychiatric scenarios.
links.quote: Safety risks were most prominent in overdose, critical care, and psychiatric scenarios.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation by 47 clinicians reviewing LLM outputs across standardized clinical vignettes for safety, hallucinations, and bias.
